findings.title: The main branch of holiman/uint256 replaces division and remainder on the path every go-ethereum family network takes, and no client pins it yet
findings.difference: holiman/uint256 master de2a038 (2026-11-22, proxy version v1.3.3-0.20261122165954-de2a0381370e) adds a power-of-two shortcut to Div, new register-only routines udiv and umod with one Knuth step per divisor size (rem5by4, rem4by3, quoRem4by3, rem3by2), and rewrites SDiv, SMod, Slt, Sgt, Eq, WriteToSlice and PaddedBytes. Mod is now umod, and MulMod and AddMod reach it whenever the product or sum fits in 256 bits. go-ethereum master bbafd66, bor develop, bsc develop, celo-org/op-geth master, OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master and nitro master all still require v1.3.2, and avalanchego 1.15.3 and libevm main require v1.2.4.
findings.mechanism: 1. The PoolManager reaches these routines on every swap and liquidity change: DIV and MOD in UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp and TickMath, SDIV and SMOD in TickBitmap.compress and flipTick, MULMOD in FullMath.mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp, SLT and SGT in the tick checks. 2. When a client bumps its uint256 requirement, the go-ethereum handlers call the new code with the same operand aliasing as today (y.Div(x, y), z.MulMod(x, y, z), instructions.go of go-ethereum master). 3. A fault in the new Knuth steps would change a quotient or a remainder for divisors of a particular limb count, which would change prices, amounts and tick indexes in mined blocks on that network. 4. This cycle built v1.3.2 and master with the local go1.24.7 and ran 1,845,864 vectors through both, with the aliasing of the go-ethereum handlers, against Python integers: no mismatch in either. The set includes every edge pair, every power of two and its neighbours as divisor, divisors of one to four limbs with the top limb normalised and not, quotients at a limb boundary, FullMath shapes and the 21,537 MULMOD and ADDMOD records of cycle 25. Three planted faults that change results were caught (6, 669 and 26,444 mismatches); a fourth planted change turned out to be equivalent and changes nothing.
findings.impact: None today. No network runs the new code. If a release adopts it with a fault the tests above missed, every pool on that network would compute different amounts from other clients and from the reference, which is a consensus split before it is a loss to any user.
findings.preconditions: A client release that requires a uint256 version later than v1.3.2. None does as of 2026-11-27.
findings.mitigations: Rerun scripts/u256vectors.py of this work directory against the uint256 version of each geth-family release before deployment, and the battery and targeted sets against an endpoint that runs it.

the v1.3.2 routines that every client pins

cleared.check: L-1171, go-ethereum master: does core/vm at bbafd66 (2026-11-25) hold an operand, result, reciprocal or jump destination cache that could return a value keyed on fewer bits than its input? Read instructions.go, interpreter.go, the generated loop interpreter_gen.go, jump_table.go, stack.go, memory.go, contract.go, jumpdests.go, evm.go and contracts.go, and every file of core/vm in the module archive, which lists precompile_cache.go (copyright 2026) as the newest addition.
cleared.result: No arithmetic cache. Every arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND and EXP handler calls the stock uint256 v1.3.2 routine on the stack words (opMulmod is z.MulMod(x, y, z)). opKeccak256 hashes the memory slice each time with no cache. The jump destination cache (jumpdests.go, a map and a layered map) is keyed by the full code hash and stores the bitmap computed from that code. The precompile result cache keys an entry by the fork table pointer, the precompile address and the precompile input or its normalised prefix, stores only results that returned no error, charges gas before the lookup on hit and on miss, and returns a copy. The PoolManager reaches a precompile only when a caller names a precompile address as a currency or a native recipient (P1 to P3 of ASSUMPTIONS.md), and the precompiles that opt in are pure functions of the bytes kept in the key, so a hit returns what a fresh run would; whether a normalisation drops a byte that matters is a question for each precompile and is not one of PoolManager arithmetic. The generated loop was checked case by case: for 70 opcodes the underflow bound, overflow bound, static gas and stack change equal the specification (scripts/genloop.py), DUP and SWAP use n and n+1 as bounds, and every case calls the same handler as the table loop. instructions.go and interpreter_gen.go are byte-identical to release v1.17.10, which Ethereum geth nodes ran in the cycle 29 ethereum-reference unit; between v1.17.10 and master, core/vm changed only by removing the verkle table and in tracer, gas and precompile files.

cleared.check: L-1171, forks: do bor develop, bsc develop, ava-labs/libevm main, celo-org/op-geth master or OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master put a cache or a different routine in front of DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, the shifts, the comparisons, KECCAK256, MLOAD, SLOAD or JUMPI?
cleared.result: Only bor does, as recorded before. The handler bodies of 45 instructions were extracted from each fork and compared with go-ethereum master (scripts/handlers.py). All five forks call the same uint256 routine with the same aliasing; they differ only in the older pop and peek calls and the interpreter receiver. bor routes MULMOD with a modulus of four limbs through mulmod_memo.go, which reuses a reciprocal only when all four limbs of the modulus equal the stored ones (mm.mod != *z compares the whole array) and lives in one EVM, and puts a 64 byte keccak cache in front of KECCAK256 keyed by the whole input (cleared in cycle 26). This cycle compiled bor develop mulmod_memo.go (sha256 9a721f0c) unchanged into a harness with one memo for the whole run and sent all 1,845,864 vectors through it in sequence, including 100,426 MULMOD with moduli changing between neighbours: 0 mismatches. libevm keeps opAddmod with a zero check in front of the same AddMod and pins uint256 v1.2.4, whose routines cycle 26 read. OffchainLabs master hashes through a hasher on the EVM, as go-ethereum did before. The commit that Nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 names (b72783f, the build that arb1.arbitrum.io and Robinhood Chain answer with on 2026-11-27) is still not published: the tag v3.13.0-rc.9 and the commit both return 404 on raw.githubusercontent.com, so its go-ethereum submodule could not be read.

cleared.check: L-1171, holiman/uint256: did MulMod, AddMod, Div, SDiv, Mod, SMod, Exp, the shifts, Byte or ExtendSign change after v1.3.2, and does any version behave differently from the specification when called the way go-ethereum calls it?
cleared.result: On master de2a038 Div, Mod, SDiv, SMod, Slt, Sgt, Eq, WriteToSlice and PaddedBytes changed; MulMod, AddMod, Exp, Lsh, Rsh, SRsh, Byte and ExtendSign did not, except that MulMod and AddMod now reach the new Mod. The new code was read: the power-of-two test is y0&(y0-1)==0 followed by a check that the remaining limbs hold one bit, which Go precedence evaluates as intended; udiv and umod read every limb of the divisor into locals before writing z, so the aliasing z == y of the handlers is safe; a normalisation shift of zero gives x >> 64 == 0 under Go shift rules; each Knuth step adds back while the top limb is nonzero, which bounds the add-backs at two. 1,845,864 vectors gave 0 mismatches on v1.3.2 and on master (seed 29_2026_11_27). The new code is in no release and no client requires it (finding of this unit).

cleared.check: L-1173: compiler fixes made after go1.25.12 (2026-07-07) that touch prove, branchelim, dead store elimination, bounds check elimination, the amd64 and arm64 rules or the math/bits intrinsics, whether go1.25.12 carries each, and whether the faulty shape occurs in core/vm or uint256 v1.3.2.
cleared.result: The release branches list these compiler fixes after go1.25.12. In go1.25.13 and not in go1.25.12: prove "time traveling proofs" (f59f3cc352, issue 80517, with its prerequisite bff0502b40), prove Const64 slice masks for slices above 4 GB (271e96aab9), mergelocals address analysis (83933547d8), a DWARF assertion in dead code (5720c29c93, a compile failure), plus riscv64 and mips fixes. Only in go1.26.x and go1.27.x, never backported because go1.25 ended with go1.25.14: generic shift rules that give a Const64 count the shift type (0fbac84598, issue 81869; the faulty rules are at lines 380-410 of generic.rules in go1.25.12), dead store elimination with CondSelect (c7bed29e83, issue 81863; deadstore.go of go1.25.12 never mentions CondSelect and the fix says the shape only exists since two later CLs), an x86 assembler loop on PCALIGN (6eb58b4551, a build hang), a 32 bit rotate rule, and a simd jump table index (b7cc93a369, GOEXPERIMENT=simd). go1.25.11 already fixed the amd64 x+x<<63 rule (917b60b494), so go1.25.12 has it. Shapes: a go/types scan of uint256 v1.3.2 finds no shift whose count has an 8, 16 or 32 bit type, no recover, and signed division or remainder only on loop indices that start at zero (uint256.go:143, :304), on the byte sign shift of ExtendSign (:1284) and in Sqrt and Dec, which the EVM does not use; the prove fault needs a negative value that a later check rejects with a panic that is then recovered. The scanned core/vm files have signed division only on non-negative values (analysis_legacy.go:68, the EIP-8024 decoders) and in precompiles. Elysium then answered 40,000 vectors (seeds 29_2026_11_27 and 29_99901) aimed at signed division and remainder, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, the shifts, BYTE and the Knuth limits, in 100 batches, each bracketed by web3_clientVersion before and after: every bracket read nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12 and there was no mismatch.

cleared.check: L-1176, bytecode walk: is the slot operand of every SSTORE, SLOAD, TSTORE and TLOAD of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json a constant, a KECCAK256 output, or a KECCAK256 output plus a constant below 8, with no multiplication, shift or caller-supplied addend on the path?
cleared.result: Yes. The runtime has 148 such sites (79 SLOAD, 40 SSTORE, 20 TLOAD, 9 TSTORE). A provenance-tracking copy of the reference interpreter (taintevm.py) ran script sets 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 (1705 scripts, 503,596,568 steps) and tagged every stack and memory word as constant, keccak output, keccak plus constant, or other. 148 sites ran. Persistent slots are the constants 0, 2 (owner, protocolFeeController) or keccak outputs, or keccak outputs plus 1, 2 or 3 (the largest offset seen is 3: feeGrowthGlobal0, feeGrowthGlobal1 and liquidity of a pool, the two fee growth words of a tick, the two fee words of a position). The +4, +5 and +6 of ticks, tickBitmap and positions appear only inside the preimage of a second keccak. Transient slots are the four constants of Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyReserves or the keccak of the CurrencyDelta pair. No slot is built with MUL, a shift or an addend that is not a PUSH constant. Every site ran. The five sites that only script set 6 reaches (pc 774, 1065, 1177, 1232 and 2783) were also read in the disassembly: the four ERC-6909 allowance sites take the slot straight from a KECCAK256 one instruction before, and pc 2783 stores to the PUSH32 constant CURRENCY_SLOT. The sites whose slot is caller data are the extsload and exttload readers (pc 2343, 2483, 2917, 9783, 10702), which only read. No write can reach the bit-248 partner of another write except by two keccak outputs, or a keccak output and a small constant, that differ in bit 248 alone after an offset of at most 3: about 2^128 hash evaluations for a collision between two attacker-chosen families and 2^256 to hit a given victim slot. The attacker has ample input freedom (pool keys, tick and word indexes, position owner and salt, ERC-6909 owner and id), and a collision between its own ERC-6909 balance and one of its tick words would mint claims, but the work is out of reach.

cleared.check: L-1176 on chain: on Avalanche, is a storage write to slot s read back at s xor 2^248, does the same hold for other high bits, and does TSTORE alias? Polygon and BNB Chain as controls.
cleared.result: On Avalanche (avalanchego/1.15.3 commit 983815fd, read before and after) a write to each of 14 slots (the fixed slots 0 to 6 and PoolManager-shaped pool, tick, bitmap, position and ERC-6909 slots) is read back at s xor 2^248 in 14 of 14 cases and at no other mask tried (2^249, 2^255, 0xff << 248, 2^247, 1). TSTORE and TLOAD do not alias for any mask. Polygon (bor v2.11.1-private) and BNB Chain (Geth v1.8.2) show no alias. Since the PoolManager reads and writes each of its slots under the same index, the fold maps each slot to one trie key and changes nothing unless two of its slots fold together, which the bytecode walk above rules out.

leads.question: When go-ethereum, bor, bsc, Nitro, libevm or celo op-geth first requires a holiman/uint256 version after v1.3.2, do the vectors of scripts/u256vectors.py and the battery still give 0 mismatches on that version and on an endpoint that runs it?
leads.why: The unreleased master rewrites Div and Mod, which every swap reaches through DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD and MULMOD.

leads.question: Once Nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 (commit b72783f) or its go-ethereum submodule is published, does its core/vm add any cache or routine in front of the arithmetic handlers?
leads.why: The build that answers Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain is still unpublished, so its interpreter has only been tested through its answers.

leadResults.answer: go-ethereum master bbafd66 has no arithmetic cache; its new caches key jump destinations by code hash and precompile results by fork, address and input. bor develop still has the only arithmetic cache, keyed on all four modulus limbs, and its source gave 0 mismatches on 1,845,864 vectors in one long sequence. bsc develop, libevm main, celo op-geth master and OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master call the stock routines. holiman/uint256 master rewrites division and remainder but no client requires it (new finding, information). The Nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 commit b72783f is still unpublished, so the build behind Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain was not read; it was tested through its answers in earlier cycles.

Eight compiler fixes after go1.25.12 touch generic or amd64 code. The three that can miscompile on amd64 (prove time travel, prove slice masks above 4 GB, typed shift-count constants) need a negative value rejected later by a recovered panic, a slice above 4 GB, or a shift count of an 8, 16 or 32 bit type, none of which occurs in uint256 v1.3.2 or the core/vm files read. Elysium returned the reference word on 40,000 aimed vectors, every batch bracketed by nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12.

All 148 storage and transient storage sites of the build take a constant, a keccak output or a keccak output plus at most 3 as slot, apart from the read-only extsload and exttload; 148 were confirmed by provenance tracking and the rest by disassembly. Avalanche folds s and s xor 2^248 for storage only, confirmed by eth_call. Two PoolManager slots fold together only through a 2^128 keccak collision search.
